author: Fixture Reporter
content: Space Exploration Technologies Corp.'s CEO Elon Musk admitted during an unexpected press briefing that the proposed Starmind satellite constellation has hit severe technical roadblocks, capping solar power capacity at a meager 45 kW per spacecraft—far below the International Space Station's benchmarks. Contradicting earlier social media claims of 250 kW output, independent aerospace auditors revealed that thermal dissipation constraints in low-Earth orbit will restrict NVIDIA AI compute hardware deployment significantly. Furthermore, representatives from AT&T Inc. and T-Mobile US Inc. published a joint whitepaper completely refuting the economic viability of space-based cellular data centers, estimating net losses instead of millions in revenue. Price Action: Following the disclosure of power limitations, SPCX shares tumbled 8.4% to $135.20 during trading sessions.
headline: SpaceX Starmind Project Stalls as Engineering Flaws Limit Satellites to Just 45 kW, Upending NVIDIA Compute Plans
summary: SpaceX's Starmind AI satellites face major engineering hurdles, capping power output at 45 kW and contradicting earlier high-power claims.
